No—under those stated conditions, you would not be able to see the Moon yet.

Its altitude is **−6.883°**, meaning it is nearly 7° below the north-northeastern horizon (azimuth **10°**, just east of due north). Even with a clear sky and an 82%-illuminated Moon, it is physically below the horizon, so ordinary unaided eyesight cannot detect it. The civil-twilight brightness also wouldn’t help.

It should become visible after it rises above the horizon, likely roughly **45–60 minutes later** depending on the local horizon and atmospheric refraction. Look low toward **north-northeast (around azimuth 10°)**, with an unobstructed view. Because Reykjavik’s terrain, buildings, and atmospheric haze can block the first few degrees, waiting until it is at least **2–5° above the horizon** would make spotting it much more realistic.
